title: Isolation of mouse mammary carcinoma-derived macrophages and cancer cells for co-culture assays
protocol: Isolate macrophages and cancer cells from mouse primary mammary carcinomas.
Mechanically dissociate the primary tumors of MMTV-PyMT mice.
Digest the tumors with a collagenase/hyaluronidase solution containing DNase I at 37°C for 45 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 450 × g to separate supernatant and pellet.
Collect the supernatant containing immune cells and single cancer cells.
Enrich CD11b+ cells from the supernatant using CD11b MicroBeads.
Allow CD11b+ cells to adhere to a fibronectin-coated glass bottom plate for 1 hour.
Remove non-adherent cells by washing with PBS after 1 hour.
Isolate cancer cells from the tumor cell pellets.
Dissociate the cell aggregates into single cancer cells using TrypLE Express Enzyme containing DNase I at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Choose the size of the tumor according to your purpose, such as an early-stage tumor (tumor size <5 mm) or an advanced-stage tumor (tumor size >12 mm).
Use dissociation buffer and TrypLE Express Enzyme to process tumors based on their weight.
Centrifuge tubes containing processed tumors at 450 × g with pulse centrifugation settings of acceleration/deceleration at 9/9 for immediate separation of single cells from cell aggregates.
Perform pulse centrifugation to isolate immune and cancer cells from the same tumors simultaneously.
Collect immune cells from the supernatant.
Collect cancer cells from the pellet.
Thaw 10× collagenase/hyaluronidase and warm up 1% BSA solution to 20°C–25°C.
Place one 10 cm Petri dish with cold PBS on ice.
Disinfect the dissection station with 70% ethanol.
Clean surgical supplies, a dissection board covered with a sterile blue pad, and pins with 70% ethanol.
Heat sterilize surgery tools at 280°C for 1 min using a glass bead sterilizer.
Cool sterilized tools on the blue pad.
Euthanize the mouse in a CO2-saturated chamber followed by cervical dislocation.
Pin the carcass to the dissection board with its back up.
Spray the carcass with 70% ethanol until wet.
Make an incision on the abdominal skin and extend it along the ventral midline towards the neck, being careful not to cut the peritoneum.
Use tweezers and a cotton swab to release the skin from the peritoneum.
Pull the skin away and stretch it tight before pinning it down.
Collect and pool primary tumors in the Petri dish.
Avoid collecting lymph nodes during dissection to ensure optimal tumor-associated macrophage purity and yield.
Do not collect necrotic tumors as they contain high percentages of neutrophils.
Remove fat and vessels around the tumor to avoid increased ACK lysis time and potential cell damage.
Transfer dissected tumors to a tissue culture hood for further processing.
Digest tumors with dissociation buffer for proper cellular isolation.
Pre-coat pipettes with 1% BSA solution before use to increase cellular yield from tumor tissues.
Prepare the dissociation buffer as described in materials and equipment.
Turn on the 37°C shaker.
Rinse the tumors with PBS.
Transfer the rinsed tumors to a new 10 cm Petri dish.
Add 1 mL of dissociation buffer to the tumors.
Mince the tumors with a sterilized razor blade until paste-like.
Transfer the minced tissue into a 50 mL tube using a 10 mL pipette pre-coated with 0.1% BSA.
Digest the minced tumors in a 37°C shaker horizontally for 45 minutes at a speed of 20 cycles per minute.
Centrifuge the digested tumors.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet with wash buffer.
Use pulse centrifugation to harvest the unclear supernatant for macrophage isolation.
Repeat pulse centrifugation until the supernatant is clear, and then collect the pellet for cancer cell isolation.
Cut tumors into small pieces with a razor blade until they are paste-like.
Transfer minced tissue into a 50 mL tube with a BSA-coated 10 mL pipette.
Place the tube horizontally in a 37°C shaker to ensure even mixing.
Shake for 45 minutes at a speed of 20 cycles per minute.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down about 30 times using a BSA-coated 5 mL pipette.
Add 10 mL of wash buffer to each 50 mL tube.
Resuspend cells completely.
Spin down cells at 450 × g for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 mL of wash buffer.
Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Pulse to 450 × g.
Collect the supernatant for macrophage isolation.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of wash buffer.
Repeat wash/pulse spins until the supernatant is clear.
Pool all non-clear supernatants in one 50 mL tube.
Wash the pellet with 10 mL of PBS to remove residual FBS from the wash buffer.
Spin down cells at 450 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of TrypLE Express Enzyme.
Add 2 μL DNase I (final concentration 4 U/mL).
Incubate the 15 mL tube horizontally in the 37°C shaker for 10 minutes at a speed of 20 cycles per minute.
Digest the pellet with TrypLE Express Enzyme in the 37°C shaker for 10 minutes at a speed of 20 cycles per minute.
Add 9–10 mL of wash buffer to each 15 mL tube after digestion.
Spin down the cells at 450 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully without touching the pellet.
Wash the pellet with 10 mL of wash buffer.
Spin down the cells at 450 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in wash buffer.
Transfer the suspension to a 50 mL falcon tube.
Adjust the volume of the suspension to 20–30 mL with additional wash buffer.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL tube.
Filter the cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer into another new 50 mL tube.
Count the cells in the filtered suspension.
Spin down 5 × 10^6 cancer cells at 450 × g for 5 minutes.
Plate the spun-down cells onto one 10 cm tissue culture dish.
Add 12 mL of cancer cell culture medium to the plate.
Culture the cells for 12–16 hours in an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Spin down the collected, pooled supernatant at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5–10 mL of cold ACK lysis buffer to lyse erythrocytes.
Incubate on ice for 5–10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant after ACK lysis.
Filter the cell suspension with a pre-separation filter.
Load cells onto the LS column after incubation with microbeads.
Wash away magnetically unlabeled antibody cells.
Firmly apply the plunger to flush out the magnetically labeled antibody cells.
Determine the percentage of CD11b+ cells (CD45+CD11b+) by flow cytometry after magnetic separation.
Culture CD11b+ cells in the incubator for 1 hour to allow macrophages to attach.
Determine the purity of macrophages (CD45+F4/80+) by flow cytometry.
Observe the morphology of macrophages.
Filter the cell suspension through a 30 μm pre-separation filter to a new 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Pipette off the supernatant completely.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 90 μL of MACS buffer per 10^7 total cells.
Vortex CD11b MicroBeads thoroughly before use.
Add 10 μL of CD11b MicroBeads per 10^7 total cells.
Mix well and incubate for 15 min at 4–8°C.
Wash cells by adding 1–2 mL of buffer per 10^7 cells.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Pipette off the supernatant completely.
Resuspend up to 10^8 cells in 500 μL of MACS buffer.
Place the LS column in the magnetic field of the MACS separator.
Rinse the LS column with 3 mL of MACS buffer.
Load the cell suspension onto the column.
Wash the column three times with MACS buffer.
Add MACS buffer to the column reservoir each time it becomes empty.
Place the column partially in a new 15 mL collection tube.
Pipette 5 mL of MACS buffer onto the column.
Firmly apply the plunger supplied with the column to flush out the fraction containing magnetically labeled cells.
Count the collected cells.
Stain cells with BV785™ anti-mouse CD45 antibody and APC anti-mouse/human CD11b antibody for flow cytometry (optional).
Pre-coat a 24-well glass bottom plate with fibronectin during centrifugation.
Dilute fibronectin in PBS to a concentration of 10 μg/mL.
Add 300 μL of diluted fibronectin to each well.
Incubate the plate for 45 min–1 h at 37°C (or pre-coat for 12–16 h at 4°C).
Store fibronectin-coated plates for up to 2–4 weeks at 4°C in a sterile container or bag.
Warm up the macrophage culture medium to 20°C–25°C.
Add fresh 2-mercaptoethanol to the medium, final concentration: 55 μM.
Add fresh M-CSF to the medium, final concentration: 10 ng/mL.
Centrifuge the CD11b+ cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Pipette off the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of macrophage culture medium per 6 × 10^5 cells.
Carefully aspirate the remaining fibronectin solution from the plate.
Rinse the plate once with PBS.
Culture CD11b+ cells in the incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 (6 × 10^5 CD11b+ cells per well).
After 1 hour of attachment, remove the unattached cells by pipetting out the supernatant.
Wash the attached cells 3 times with PBS to remove any remaining leukocytes.
Detach adherent cells with Trysin+0.5 M EDTA at 37°C until the cells become round (∼10 min).
Scrape the round cells (macrophages) gently with a cell lifter.
Stain 1–2 × 10^6 cells with BV785™ anti-mouse CD45 antibody and Alexa Fluor® 488 anti-mouse F4/80 antibody for flow cytometry.
Culture the macrophages for 12–16 h in the incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Detach cancer cells from the tissue culture dish using TrypLE Express Enzyme.
Label detached cancer cells with CellTracker™ CMFDA Dye at a concentration of 1 μM.
Label macrophages with CellTracker™ Deep Red Dye at a concentration of 1 μM.
Seed labeled cancer cells onto a 24-well glass bottom plate where macrophages are cultured.
Allow seeded cancer cells to attach for 2 hours.
Prepare MPLA stock solution by diluting it from 100 μg/mL in 0.2% triethylamine to the final concentration of 100 ng/mL.
Prepare IFNγ stock solution by diluting it from 100 μg/mL in PBS to the final concentration of 33 ng/mL.
Prepare vehicle solution containing 0.2% × 10−3 triethylamine.
Apply different treatments (vehicle/MPLA+IFNγ/MPLA/IFNγ) to the co-culture system after cancer cells have attached for 2 hours.
Aspirate the medium from the cancer cell culture dish.
Wash with PBS to remove residual FBS.
Add 3 mL of TrypLE Express Enzyme to a 10 cm dish.
Incubate for 5–10 min at 37°C until cells detach when rocked.
Add FBS to stop TrypLE Express Enzyme digestion.
Spin down the cancer cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in serum-free DMEM.
Count the cells.
Dilute the cancer cells to 1.5 × 10^5 per 500 μL of serum-free medium.
Add CMFDA Dye to the cells at a final concentration of 1 μM and mix gently up and down 3–5 times.
Stain for 30 min in the incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Add at least 3 volumes of FBS to the stained cancer cells.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the cancer cell culture medium.
Stain the macrophages with CellTracker™ Deep Red Dye.
Aspirate the macrophage culture medium from the 24-well plate.
Wash with PBS once.
Add the Deep Red Dye working solution to the macrophages (500 μL per well).
Stain the macrophages for 30 min in the incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Add at least 3 volumes of FBS to the stained macrophages and aspirate the solution.
Add fresh macrophage culture medium to the plate (500 μL per well).
Seed the cancer cells to the 24-well plate.
Seed 5 × 10^4 cancer cells in 500 μL of cancer cell culture medium per well.
After 2 h of attachment, add 1 mL of macrophage culture medium to each well (for 2 mL medium in total for each well).

To test the effects of macrophage activating drugs, add e.g., MPLA or IFNγ alone or in combination to the 1 mL of macrophage medium so that the final concentration (in 2 mL) is 100 ng/mL of MPLA and/or 33 ng/mL of IFNγ.
Set up the LiveCellTM Stage Top Incubation System.
Place the co-cultured 24-well plate on the stage and turn on the incubation system.
Wait until the system is stabilized at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 75-85% relative humidity for approximately 2 hours.
Use a thermometer to ensure the temperature does not exceed 38°C.
Check that there is sufficient CO2 for continuous imaging over 3 days.
Operate the Yokogawa spinning disk confocal microscope.
While waiting for system stabilization, select five fields of view per well.
Start time-lapse imaging when the incubation system reaches optimal conditions.
Take images every 20 minutes for a total duration of 60 hours.
